$comment: Mutation definitions for spec 009 (in-page autofill overlay).
This file is the mutation table. It used to live in PR bodies, where it
drifted twice: a stale kill count in #37, and a Slice A2 row (A2-M4,
registration-id injectivity) that survived with ZERO kills for a full slice
because the property was asserted only in a code comment.
Each mutation names a security property, the literal edits that break it,
and the number of tests that must die. `expectedKills` is measured, never
guessed: run the runner, read the number, pin it here. A drifted number is
reported as a failure, which is the whole point of committing this file.
`find` is matched as a LITERAL string, never a regex, and must match exactly
`expect` times (default 1). A definition that matches nothing is a hard
error, not a silent pass.
WHY THESE NUMBERS DIFFER FROM THE PR BODIES
If you are comparing this file against the tables in PR #40, #47 or #50 and
the numbers disagree: THIS FILE IS THE REFERENCE. The tables are snapshots
of a suite that no longer exists. Three known, deliberate divergences:
* EVERY A0 ROW. PR #40 measured against a 100-test Node suite. Slice A2
grew it to 179 (content_overlay behavioural tests via fake_page.js, and
the crash-injection cases), and closing the A2-M7 survivor made it 180.
The A0 mutations were not weakened and the A0 policy did not change —
there are simply more tests in the blast radius. A0 counts going UP
against #40 is expected; going DOWN is a regression worth chasing.
* A2-M4. PR #50 recorded '4 kills'. That was a UNIT ERROR: 4 assertions
inside ONE test case. This runner counts test cases, so 1 is correct.
See the row's own comment.
* A0-M2, A4-M8, A4-M9 and A5-M6 went UP again in the A7 slice (240→241,
9→10, 42→48, 4→8). Same cause as the A0 rows above: the M7 iframe→
iframe tests widened the blast radius of mutations that were already
strong. No mutation was weakened and no policy changed.
* A1-M2. PR #47 recorded 14, this file measures 10, because the mutation
here is a tighter reconstruction and the Flutter suite is targeted at
four files. See the row's own comment.
* EVERY A0 ROW AGAIN, PLUS A2-M9/M12/M13, IN SLICE A3. The Node suite went
from 180 to 237 tests (overlay_routes.test.js). None of these mutations
was weakened and no policy was relaxed — the blast radius simply grew,
and several of them now die in the router tests as well as the unit ones.
Two rows were RETARGETED because A3 rewrote the code under them, and both
got wider rather than narrower: A2-M6 (the durable commit now reads back
the revision floor too) and A2-M12 (the reconciliation gate moved from
authorizeBootstrap to authorizeContentRequest, covering all three content
routes instead of one). A2-M11 remains declared-equivalent; its reason was
rewritten because A023 made the branch explicitly refused rather than
incidentally unread.
* A0-M2, A0-M7, A2-M9, A3-M1, A3-M3, A3-M6, IN SLICE A4. The Node suite
went from 249 to 286 tests (overlay_session.test.js and
secret_lifetime.test.js drive the shipped content overlay end to end).
None of these mutations was weakened — broken canonicalization, grant
replay, route collapse and binding trust now also kill the new
content-side tests. Blast radius only.

* A0-M1, A0-M2, A0-M4, A3-M1, A2-M15, A2-M16, WITH THE PENDING-INTENT FIX. The Node suite went from 337 to 347 tests. Measured post-merge with the #75 polish suite: 352 tests total (342 polish + 10 intent); A0-M2 re-pinned at 223, the union of both branches' growth, re-measured by the runner rather than summed by hand (overlay_enable_intent.test.js: the macOS grant race where the permission prompt closes the popup). None of these mutations was weakened — broken canonicalization, route collapse, the re-enabled onAdded sweep and the order-sensitive readback now also kill the intent-path tests, which drive permissions.request, onAdded and enableOrigin end to end. Blast radius only.
The general rule: a number in a PR body was true once and is now unowned;
a number in this file is re-measured on every run and fails the build when
it drifts. Do not 'correct' this file to match a PR — re-run the runner.

* A0-M2, A4-M4, A4-M6, A4-M8, A4-M9, IN SLICE A5. The Node suite went from 286 to 306 tests (overlay_interaction.test.js and the five required A039 named DOM assertions in content_overlay.test.js). None of these mutations was weakened — broken canonicalization, submit-on-fill, DOM-visible entry ids, surviving watchdogs and surviving hosts now also kill the new interaction and geometry tests. Blast radius only. A4-M10 was RETARGETED: A038 replaced the anonymous mousedown preventDefault with the named markPendingAction handler, so the mutation now removes the preventDefault inside it; the property (pointer-down must not steal anchor focus) is unchanged and the kill set got wider, not narrower.

* A0-M2, A2-M9, A3-M1, A4-M4, A4-M9, A5-M6, A5-M8, IN SLICE A6 (A040). The Node suite went from 353 to 368 tests (overlay_at_activation.test.js plus the extended light-DOM A032 scan). None of these mutations was weakened — the new AT-activation and light-fallback tests sit in their blast radius. A4-M10 is the one deliberate NARROWING: A040 makes DOM focus entering the overlay a survivable event by design (the focusin handler cancels the deferred outside-blur teardown), so the mutant that lets mousedown steal the anchor focus no longer cascades into mass teardown-before-click failures — the overlay now survives that focus move on purpose. The property (pointer-down must not steal anchor focus) is still pinned by the direct A038 assertions; 3 kills, re-measured.
SLICE C — THE PER-ORIGIN OPT-IN BECAME ONE GLOBAL SWITCH.
Product decision, taken by the user: the per-site 'Turn on' click was
unusable in practice. `overlayConfigV1 {version, revision, enabledOrigins[]}`
is replaced by `overlayConfigV2 {version, revision, enabled}` under a new
storage key; the popup asks once for the broad optional host permission.
WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, and is asserted here rather than assumed: the MANIFEST.
A015 still holds — no mandatory `host_permissions`, the broad pair is still
only `optional_host_permissions`, still granted under a popup gesture. Only
the runtime ASK changed shape. Exact-origin authorization for REVEALING a
credential is likewise untouched: sender-derived origin, exact-origin native
query, one-shot tokens, the databaseId/cacheGeneration/bridgeGeneration
triple, isTrusted, closed shadow root, log sanitizer and teardown are all
unchanged. Slice C changed WHERE the script is injected, not what it may show.
Eight rows were rewritten because the code moved under them. Each carries an
explicit verdict in its own $comment:
ADAPTED (same property, new code): A0-M6, A2-M1, A2-M3, A2-M5, A2-M8,
A2-M9, A2-M13, A2-M11 (still declared-equivalent).
SUBSTITUTED (the old property has no subject; a named successor takes its
job): A2-M17 (intent origin -> grant sufficiency), A5-M4 (top-lends-
authorization -> unresolvable top must not be guessed as agreeing).
Seven NEW rows, C-M1..C-M7, cover invariants that did not exist before:
the v1->v2 migration must start DISABLED (C-M1 in the lifecycle, C-M2 in the
parser — two independent gates, one mutation each), the broad grant must be
re-checked per request (C-M3), disable must hand back the permission (C-M4)
and drop the registration (C-M5), the grant is checked as a SET not a member
(C-M6), and the switch is fail-closed on its TYPE (C-M7).
PROPERTIES RETIRED, with reasons, because they have no subject left — not
because the code changed shape. All were per-origin bookkeeping:
* permission/registration refcounting across origins that share one
Chromium pattern (two ports of a host). One switch, no sharing.
* `unsupported_origin` and `too_many_origins`: `enable()` takes no origin
and a boolean has no length, so neither refusal has a producer. Both
were removed from the public error mapping in the same commit.
* 'an injected sibling port stays inert': the global switch enables it by
design. Exact-origin BINDING, the half that protects the credential, is
still pinned by A0-M6, A3-M2 and the router's exact-origin query tests.
COUNTS THAT WENT DOWN, and why that is not a regression here: A0-M1 47->34,
lost kills to the retired per-origin tests above, which is the mechanical
consequence of deleting tests for a model that no longer exists. No mutation
was weakened and no assertion was relaxed to make a number move. Counts that
blast-radius growth from the new migration and global-lifecycle tests.
TWO MUTATIONS SURVIVED WHEN FIRST MEASURED, and both survived for the same
instructive reason: a SECOND, independent defence masked them. C-M1's bad
migration was masked by the fail-closed grant check in reconcile, and
A2-M17's over-broad grant acceptance was masked by `enable`'s own
permissions.contains re-check. Defence in depth is the right design and was
kept; the tests were rewritten to construct the state where only the
property under test can refuse (broad grant already held, no pruning
reconcile in between). Both kill now.
SLICE C POST-REVIEW (finding 1). C-M8 was added after review found that the
partial-external-revoke test asserted the config, the registrations and the
teardown but NOT the granted permissions — so the orphan sweep on the
reconcile path had no mutation behind it, while C-M4 covered only the
disable path's D5. The missing assertion was added in the same commit; the
counterfactual was run (mutant applied, assertion removed) and confirms the
target test passes without it, so the assertion is load-bearing rather than
riding on C-M8's other kills.
SLICE A8 — MV3 ORPHANED CONTENT-SCRIPT INSTANCE (manual QA, CDP trace).
The extension was reloaded while a login page stayed open. Chrome does not
notify the injected content script; it removes the API bridge underneath it,
so `chrome.runtime` reads back `undefined`. Enter on the Generate row hit
`chrome.runtime.sendMessage` and the ACCESS threw
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sendMessage')`.
The overlay died in silence. Reported as "I can't select an entry with the
keyboard any more" — the arrows were fine, the ACTION was dead.
The `lastError` branch each callback already carried was no defence: it lives
inside a callback an orphan can never reach, because the access that would
schedule it is the access that throws. The fix is a sweep, not a patch at the
reported line — all 14 `chrome.*` call sites in content_overlay.js are behind
the `chrome.runtime?.id == null` probe, and A8-M4 pins the probe itself.
A8-M6 is the user-visible half: not throwing is necessary but not sufficient,
so the mutant that exits silently (no honest state) is killed separately from
the mutants that crash.
COUNTS RE-MEASURED IN SLICE A8. The Node suite went from 406 to 437 tests
(orphaned_context.test.js). A0-M2 203→222, A4-M3 1→3, A4-M4 8→9,
A4-M8 10→13, A4-M9 48→55, A5-M5 2→4, A5-M8 3→4. None was weakened:
broken canonicalization, a surviving watchdog, a surviving host and the
light-listbox leak now also kill the orphan tests, which drive focus, fill,
generate, teardown, re-injection and bootstrap end to end. Blast radius only.
A4-M9 was RETARGETED, not weakened: teardown grew a `keepHost` option with
exactly one caller (the orphan exit, which leaves an honest tombstone on
screen). The mutation still deletes the host removal outright, so the
property — teardown removes the host on every normal trigger — is unchanged.
SLICE A8 POST-REVIEW. Five findings, one blocking.
* A8-M8 (BLOCKING, regression). goInert held the bootstrap guard
unconditionally. With no `content_scripts` manifest block, every instance
arrives via registerContentScripts/executeScript, so a held guard blocks
re-injection outright. An orphan that latched inert with NO tombstone
(no session open) therefore left the tab silent AND unrecoverable — the
exact failure mode this slice exists to remove, reintroduced by its own
fix. origin/main survived the reproduced sequence, confirming a
behavioural regression rather than a pre-existing gap. The guard is now
released exactly when no tombstone was left; A8-M9 pins the other half.
* A8-M10. The tombstone was not one sentence: `generateEl` is a sibling of
the list, so clearing the rows left it alive, enabled and aria-selected
inside the notice. Nothing pinned the notice's CONTENT before this.
* A8-M11. `kv-list` kept `aria-activedescendant` after every non-match
state emptied it — a dangling IDREF on `timeout`/`locked`/`no_host` too,
not only on the orphan state.
* Doc fixes, no mutation: the guard-lifecycle comment at the top of
content_overlay.js was false after goInert (now enumerates every release
point), and the guarded-site count is 14, not 13 — the 13 pre-existing
sites plus the best-effort removeListener goInert itself added.

mutations.property: a reconciliation triggered by a permission change drops every focus grant
$comment: CLOSED. Found as a SURVIVOR by this runner on its first full execution,
and closed by the test it demanded.
Third instance of the same failure mode as A2-M4 and the content_overlay
gap: the property is stated in spec.md:296 ('first load/validate durable
config, clear all in-memory grants, then reconcile...') and repeated in a
comment above the call, and NO test asserted it.
Never a live vulnerability: an external revocation also bumps the config
revision, and FocusGrantStore.consume() rejects a grant whose
configRevision is stale. The grant clear is defence in depth — but it was
defence in depth that nothing held, which is how it silently rots.
THE TEST ASSERTS THE EFFECT, NOT THE STATE. The obvious closure — mint a
grant, reconcile, assert `worker.grants.size === 0` — was NOT written.
Inspecting the data structure is the same class of weakness as the three
gaps above: it re-states the implementation instead of the guarantee, and
would go green against any refactor that keeps the Map tidy while leaving
a token redeemable. The test redeems the token through the real
FocusGrantStore.consume() path and requires it to fail.
The setup is what makes the number mean anything: the permission is still
granted and the config is valid, so this reconcile commits nothing and the
revision does not move. That deliberately disarms the downstream
configRevision check — the very thing that made this survivor harmless —
so the ONLY remaining explanation for a rejected consume is the grant
clear. The test pins that with an explicit assertion on the revision, and
redeems a second grant BEFORE the reconcile as a control so it cannot pass
vacuously on a consume that was always going to fail.

mutations.title: registration id hex is unpadded (variable width)
mutations.property: the fixed 4-hex-digit width is what makes the encoding injective for an arbitrary code point
$comment: Found BY the runner while probing A2-M4 variants, not by reading the code.
Unpadded hex survives the A018 injectivity test because every host in that
test is ASCII, and every ASCII code point is exactly 2 hex digits — so the
variable-width encoding is still injective over the tested alphabet.
It is injective over the REACHABLE alphabet too: permission patterns are
built from canonicalized ASCII hosts (IDNA is refused fail-closed in Slice
A1), so a code point above 0xff cannot reach this function.
Recorded as equivalent rather than as a gap: the padding is defence in
depth against an input canonicalization already forbids. If IDNA support
ever lands, that argument dies and this mutation starts killing.
WHERE THE REACHABILITY ARGUMENT IS ENFORCED — check these before
believing this row is still equivalent:
* overlay_security.js, canonicalizeOrigin(): a non-ASCII host is
refused fail-closed, never folded through a mapping table.
* browser_exact_origin.dart: the Dart half refuses the same input, so
neither side can hand a non-ASCII pattern to the other.
* permissionPatternForOrigin() builds the pattern only from an already
canonicalized origin, so this function has no other input path.
This equivalence is therefore CONDITIONAL, and the condition is machine-
checked rather than trusted: `equivalent: true` with `expectedKills: 0`
makes the runner treat ANY kill as drift and fail --check. The day IDNA
lands, this row goes red on its own instead of quietly staying true-by-
accident. Do not delete the row to make that noise stop — the noise is
the feature.
mutations.equivalentReason: Patterns are derived only from canonicalized ASCII hosts, so every code point is 2 hex digits and unpadded hex stays injective. mutations.title: a request is served on the committed switch alone, without the broad grant
mutations.property: `enabled: true` is not sufficient: every content request re-checks that the browser still HOLDS the broad grant, so an externally revoked permission fails closed on the very next request rather than at the next reconcile
$comment: The durable config and the browser permission are two independent facts.
Reconciliation converges them, but a request can arrive in the window
between a chrome://extensions revoke and the next reconcile. Trusting the
config alone there serves an overlay the user has just switched off at
the browser level.

edits.replace: // mutation: the committed config is trusted as proof of the grant

mutations.title: disable does not hand the broad host permission back
mutations.property: D5: turning the overlay off revokes the optional host permission, so the extension does not keep an 'can read all sites' grant nothing justifies
$comment: Sharper under Slice C than it was under Slice A2: the retained grant is
now 'all http(s) sites', not one host. A user who turns the feature off
and still sees the browser reporting full site access has been given a
switch that does not do what it says.

mutations.title: the content-script registration survives the disable
mutations.property: D4: turning the overlay off unregisters the content script, so no page loaded afterwards is injected
$comment: `persistAcrossSessions: true` means a surviving registration is not a
leak that ends with the worker — it keeps injecting into every http(s)
page, across restarts, after the user said no. The durable config still
refuses every request, so this is not an authorization bypass; it is a
revoked feature that keeps running code in the user's pages.

mutations.title: reconcile accepts half the broad grant as the whole
mutations.property: the broad grant is checked as a SET: losing either pattern is a revocation, because a half-injected overlay is not a state the user consented to
$comment: Chrome lets a user remove host permissions individually. Verifying one
pattern leaves the overlay durably 'on' while https pages — every page
that matters for credentials — silently stop working, and the enable
path would also accept a partial grant as success.

mutations.title: the frame-support gate accepts a truthy non-boolean switch
mutations.property: fail-closed on the TYPE: only a literal `true` authorizes a frame, so a caller passing a truthy non-boolean (a salvaged string, a count) cannot classify a frame as supported
$comment: The whole authorization surface collapsed from a list to one boolean in
Slice C, which makes that boolean's TYPE load-bearing in a way it was
not before. `enabledOrigins` failed closed on anything that was not an
array of canonical origins; a bare truthiness test would accept the
string "false", a non-empty leftover array, or a count.

edits.find: if (enabled !== true) return "unsupported";
edits.replace: if (enabled === false) return "unsupported"; // mutation: truthy is enough

mutations.title: reconcile never sweeps orphan permissions
mutations.property: the orphan-permission sweep runs on the RECONCILE path too, so a permission the committed config no longer justifies is handed back even when the disable transaction was never the thing that revoked it
$comment: C-M8 covers the sweep on the RECONCILE path; C-M4 covers it on the DISABLE path (D5).
Found by review, not by the runner: the partial-external-revoke test
asserted the config, the registrations and the teardown, but not the
permissions, so that path had no mutation behind it.
The scenario it protects is specific and reachable. The user removes ONE of
the two broad patterns from chrome://extensions. `reconcile` sees the grant
is no longer whole, durably commits `enabled: false` — and the OTHER pattern
is still granted, now justified by nothing. Only this sweep hands it back.
The user would otherwise be left with an extension that still reports host
access for a feature they have switched off, which is exactly the state the
permission model is supposed to make impossible.
RELATIONSHIP TO C-M4, measured rather than asserted. An earlier draft of
this row declared `disjointFrom: [C-M4]` and claimed the two kill sets were
disjoint. THAT WAS WRONG and the runner would not have caught it, because a
disjointness claim only fails the build when it is declared: 5 of the 12
kills are shared (`A021: the clean disable and every crashed disable reach
one terminal state` and its four crash-phase subtests), since those drive
the disable AND the post-crash cold-start reconcile, so both sweeps sit on
their path. The declaration was removed instead of being weakened into
something technically true.
What is true, and is why both rows are needed: NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER.
C-M8 has 7 exclusive kills (the migration, cold-start and external-revoke
paths); C-M4 has 5 exclusive kills (the disable path's own D5 assertions).
The revoke-path test in particular is killed by C-M8 alone.
ALSO NOT A2-M15'S TWIN, though both edit the same line. A2-M15 makes the
sweep UNCONDITIONAL (breaking the onAdded grant race); this removes it
ENTIRELY. Opposite directions on one guard, and the guard needs both ends
pinned or it can be moved to either extreme unnoticed.

mutations.title: bootstrap runs the handshake without probing for an orphan
mutations.property: an instance evaluated into a world whose bridge is already gone neither speaks nor builds anything
$comment: A script can be evaluated into an already-orphaned isolated world. Without
the entry guard the very first statement of the handshake throws, and
whether any listener survives that throw is left to chance rather than
decided.

$comment: Neutralises the primitive every other guard is built on. A guard that is

mutations.title: a new session queries for matches without probing for an orphan
mutations.property: a session opened on an already-orphaned instance sends no query and renders the honest state
$comment: The realistic ordering: the extension is reloaded first, and only then does
the user click a login field. `requestMatches` is also the "Try again"
target on the stale_session state — a retry is exactly when an orphan is
most likely to be hit.

mutations.title: the orphan exit rips the overlay off screen instead of leaving an honest tombstone
mutations.property: an orphan detected during a user action leaves an honest, visible state behind — it never dies in silence
$comment: The USER-VISIBLE half of the fix, and the half a purely defensive patch
would miss. Not throwing is necessary but not sufficient: the QA report was
"no error state, no message, then unmounted". Tearing the overlay off on
the way out reproduces exactly that silent death while keeping every
no-throw assertion green.

mutations.title: the orphan exit skips listener removal whenever the context probe says lost
mutations.property: the runtime listener is unregistered whenever `removeListener` is still callable, which is not the same question as whether the context is alive
$comment: A real bug made while writing this fix, kept as a mutation. In the
`id`-undefined shape the canonical probe reports the context lost while the
API is still perfectly callable — and that is precisely the case where the
listener CAN, and therefore must, be dropped. Gating removal on the
liveness probe instead of on callability leaks the listener in the one
shape where it is removable.

mutations.title: the orphan exit holds the bootstrap guard even when it left no tombstone
mutations.property: an orphan that shows the user NOTHING must release the bootstrap guard, so a new worker can re-inject and re-serve the tab instead of stranding it
$comment: THE REGRESSION THIS SLICE SHIPPED AND REVIEW CAUGHT. This extension has no
`content_scripts` manifest block — every instance arrives through
`scripting.registerContentScripts` / `executeScript` — so a held guard is
the difference between a tab a new worker can re-serve and a tab that is
dead until the user reloads it.
Reproduced sequence: no field focused, context invalidated in the
`id`-undefined shape, teardown broadcast arrives, the instance latches inert
with NO tombstone, and the guard stays set. The user clicks the password
field and gets nothing, forever. origin/main survived this exact sequence,
so holding the guard unconditionally was a behavioural regression — silent
death reintroduced through the back door of the fix for silent death.
The release is conditional, not unconditional: A8-M9 pins the other half.

mutations.title: the orphan exit releases the bootstrap guard unconditionally
mutations.property: a tombstone on screen keeps the guard held, so no working overlay ever mounts beside a notice telling the user autofill is broken
$comment: The complement of A8-M8, and the reason the release is conditional. Freeing
the guard while a tombstone is displayed lets a re-injection mount a live
overlay next to a notice that just said the page lost its connection — two
contradictory answers on screen at once.

edits.find: if (!tombstone) clearGuard();

mutations.title: the orphan notice keeps the Generate row alive inside itself
mutations.property: the orphan notice is ONE sentence: no control survives into it that looks actionable and does nothing
$comment: Found in review by measuring the tombstone rather than trusting it.
`renderState` clears `listEl`'s children, but `generateEl` is a SIBLING
inside the section, not a child — so it survived into the notice still
reading "Generate a password — confirm the save in KeyVault.", still
`disabled=false`, still `aria-selected=true`.
A control that looks live and does nothing is precisely the micro-failure
the extension_lost state exists to abolish, so finding one INSIDE the
warning about it is the worst possible place for it. Nothing else pinned
the notice's content: the pre-existing assertions covered entry title and
service only.

mutations.title: an emptied listbox keeps pointing at the row it just deleted

$comment: `kv-list` kept `aria-activedescendant="kv-option-0"` after every non-match
state swap emptied it, so assistive tech was handed a reference to an
